studies.study_name: NEURO-TTR: A Phase 2/3 Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Study to Assess the Efficacy and Safety of ISIS 420915 in Patients With Familial Amyloid Polyneuropathy
studies.design: international, randomised, double-blind (ClinicalTrials.gov maskingInfo: QUADRUPLE - participant, care provider, investigator, outcomes assessor), placebo-controlled, parallel-group, 2:1 inotersen:placebo; 15-month (65-66 week) treatment period. Platelet monitoring was PROTOCOL-AMENDED mid-trial: after the fatal grade 4 event the schedule changed from every 2-6 weeks to weekly, with a mandatory dose pause at platelet count <75 x10^9/L until recovery to >=100 x10^9/L. Platelet outcomes therefore split into a pre-amendment and a post-amendment observation regime, which the sources report separately.
studies.phase: 2/3 (ClinicalTrials.gov designModule.phases = ['PHASE2','PHASE3']; EudraCT title 'A Phase 2/3 ...'; reported in NEJM and the EPAR as the pivotal phase 3 trial)
studies.indication: hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis with polyneuropathy (hATTR-PN / familial amyloid polyneuropathy)
studies.population: adults with stage 1 (ambulatory) or stage 2 (ambulatory with assistance) hATTR with polyneuropathy; baseline platelet count <125 x10^9/L was an exclusion criterion (FDA review PDF p160, noting only 2 enrolled subjects were below that threshold). 112 inotersen / 60 placebo.
studies.n_enrolled: 173 (ClinicalTrials.gov enrollmentInfo count 173, type ACTUAL); 172 received at least one dose and form the safety set - 112 inotersen + 60 placebo (NEJM Results: 'A total of 172 patients (112 in the inotersen group and 60 in the placebo group) received at least one dose of a trial regimen, and 139 (81%) completed the intervention period.')
studies.n_analyzed_platelet: 112 inotersen + 60 placebo for the platelet-threshold and nadir analyses (FDA Clinical Safety Review Table 24 column headers 'Inotersen 300 mg (N=112)' / placebo N=60; NEJM '60 of 112, 54%' vs '8 of 60, 13%'). Smaller denominators apply to nested subgroups and MUST NOT be read as the arm denominator: antiplatelet-antibody subgroups N=6 baseline-positive / N=22 antibody-negative / N=9 treatment-emergent-positive (Table 31, antibody testing done only in selected subjects); baseline-platelet bands N=2 (<125), N=10 (<150), N=39 (<200), N=73 (>=200) (Table 33); and Table 33 reports 13 (11.6%) with nadir <75 x10^9/L at the 28-Mar-2017 cut against Table 24's 16 (14.3%) at the 15-Sep-2017 cut. Do NOT add these 112/60 to the CS3 or pooled denominators - the 161 pooled figure already contains all 112.
studies.dose_regimen: inotersen 300 mg SC, three loading doses on alternate days in week 1 then 300 mg once weekly (ClinicalTrials.gov arm description); matching placebo on the same schedule. Protocol-permitted modifications for platelet decline: dose pause at <75 x10^9/L, and reduction to 150 mg weekly (2 patients in NEJM; reduced regimens of 150-160 mg weekly or every 2 weeks in the FDA review).
studies.duration: 65-66 weeks of dosing (15 months); NEJM primary endpoint at week 66
studies.platelet_endpoint_basis: "A higher proportion of patients in the inotersen group (60 of 112, 54%) had a confirmed decrease in the postbaseline platelet count to less than 140,000 per cubic millimeter than in the placebo group (8 of 60, 13%). Decreases in the inotersen group occurred gradually over a period of several weeks, with an onset within the first 13 weeks of dosing and a mean nadir between 3 to 6 months after treatment initiation." [Benson et al., N Engl J Med 2018;379:22-31, PMID 29972757, Results / SAFETY paragraph 3, citing Table S10 and Fig. S11 of the Supplementary Appendix]. Confirmed as a protocolised, scheduled assessment with a defined monitoring window in the FDA review: "Three (2.7%) inotersen subjects had severe thrombocytopenia (<25 x10^9/L), which can have potentially fatal bleeding complications" [FDA NDA 211172 Clinical Safety Review, narrative PDF p142] alongside Table 24 (PDF p141), which tabulates every post-baseline platelet threshold (<140, <100, <75, <50, <25 x10^9/L and >=30% / >=50% decrease from baseline) for 'Inotersen 300 mg (N=112)' against placebo (N=60). Both an on-treatment schedule (2-6 weekly, amended to weekly) and a fixed 65-66 week observation window are defined.

studies.notes: This is the single trial that most of the cluster collapses onto: 126 of 198 measurement rows (64%) are CS2 cells. They are not 126 studies and not 126 independent observations - they are dose-group/arm/threshold/subgroup/individual-subject cells of a handful of tables, chiefly FDA Clinical Safety Review Tables 24, 31, 33, 34 and 45, EPAR section 2.6, and NEJM Table 2. DEDUPLICATION APPLIED per rule 2: the NEJM publication (SRC-0B8427), the Tegsedi EPAR CS2 sections (SRC-115703), the FDA NDA 211172 Clinical Safety Review CS2 columns (SRC-6E838B) and the TEGSEDI US label Warnings section 5.1 'Study 1' figures (SRC-5C4E17) are FOUR REPORTS OF THIS ONE TRIAL, so no separate label_summary evidence unit was created - the label's 25% (<100 x10^9/L), 14% (<75 x10^9/L), 3% (<25 x10^9/L) and 3-antibody-positive-patient figures reproduce FDA review Table 24 / narrative p142 for the same 112 patients. FOUR INDIVIDUAL SEVERE CASES are carried as subject-level rows but are NOT case reports: they are trial subjects reported inside the CS2 safety review (FDA review Figure 2 and Tables 26, 27, 28 - a 35-year-old male in Argentina who died on study day 122 of intracranial haemorrhage with platelets <10 x10^9/L after 19 doses; a 45-year-old female in Italy, nadir 9 x10^9/L on day 52, recovered to 250 x10^9/L off drug plus glucocorticoid; a 69-year-old male in Brazil, nadir 5 x10^9/L on day 133, recovered to 175 x10^9/L). INTERNAL DISCREPANCIES PRESERVED, NOT SMOOTHED: >=30% decrease from baseline is 75.0% (84/112) in Table 24 but 71% in the reviewer comment after Table 34 (different analysis table and data cut); nadir <75 x10^9/L is 16 (14.3%) in Table 24 (15-Sep-2017 cut) but 13 (11.6%) in Table 33 (28-Mar-2017 cut); the dose-hold rate for the <75 x10^9/L stopping rule is 11% on EPAR p88 and 'approximately 10%' on EPAR p93/p113/p128; the PT-level AE incidence is 13% (PT 'Thrombocytopenia' alone) versus 24% (PTs 'Thrombocytopenia' + 'Platelet count decreased' combined, the figure FDA used). Nineteen of the 126 rows are placebo-arm (dose 0) cells and several are explicit tabulated zeros; those are genuine measured comparator values, not fabricated negatives.

studies.indication: hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis with polyneuropathy (hATTR-PN / familial amyloid polyneuropathy)
studies.population: adults who had completed or discontinued ISIS 420915-CS2; two non-randomised cohorts by prior assignment. A nested subgroup of 6 former CS2 placebo patients who had progressed to disease stage 3 is reported separately in the EPAR (p85).
studies.n_enrolled: 135 (ClinicalTrials.gov enrollmentInfo count 135 ACTUAL; results participantFlowModule STARTED = 85 Previous Inotersen-Inotersen + 50 Previous Placebo-Inotersen; baseline denominator BG002 = 135). DO NOT ADD THIS 134 TO CS2's 112 - the 85 inotersen-inotersen patients ARE 85 of the CS2 inotersen 112, and the integrated 'All Inotersen-Treated (CS2 and CS3)' denominator of 161 = 112 CS2 inotersen patients + 49 CS2 placebo patients newly exposed in CS3. studies.duration: up to 260 weeks per protocol; platelet rows here reflect interim exposure to the 28-Feb-2017 and 15-Sep-2017 data cuts, with grade 3/4 events first detected between week 77 and week 151 of cumulative inotersen treatment. Registry primary completion 2020-09-11.
studies.platelet_endpoint_basis: "Thrombocytopenia TEAEs including TEAEs of platelet count decreases occurred in 24.1% vs. 1.7% of subjects on inotersen and placebo, respectively in CS2 and in 25/134 subjects (18.7%) in CS3." [Tegsedi EPAR, EMA/411876/2018 (EMEA/H/C/004782), p128, section 3.4 Unfavourable effects]. The scheduled threshold assessment is tabulated per CS3 cohort: FDA NDA 211172 Clinical Safety Review Table 24 (PDF p141) gives, for 'CS3 Inotersen-Inotersen (N=85)' and 'CS3 Placebo-Inotersen (N=49)' separately, the proportions below 140, 100, 75, 50 and 25 x10^9/L and with >=30% / >=50% decrease from baseline. Duration of the thrombocytopenic state and of dose interruptions were also measured in CS3 specifically: "Duration of thrombocytopenia was 28 weeks during CS2 and 41 weeks in CS3" and "The overall duration of interruptions was longer in CS3 (8 weeks vs. 4.5 weeks in CS2)" [EPAR p93]. Weekly platelet monitoring under a defined dose-pause rule gives the defined exposure/observation window.

studies.notes: 29 of 198 rows. The open-label extension is a SEPARATE REGISTERED TRIAL from CS2 but an OVERLAPPING POPULATION, which is the single most important thing to carry forward: 85 of its 134 analysed patients are the same individuals as 85 of CS2's 112 inotersen patients. Any model that treats a CS2 row and a CS3 row as independent observations is double-counting those people. Rows assigned here are those whose values carry a CS3-only denominator (Table 24 cohort columns N=85 and N=49, the 25/134 TEAE figure, the CS3-specific 13.4% dose-pause rate, 41-week duration, 8-week interruption duration, the >53% antiplatelet-antibody prevalence, the CS3 week-39 mean -28.5% change, the 22.8% haemorrhage rate, the 20% vs 0% anti-PF4 IgM cohort split and the 4/6 stage-3-progressor subgroup). The post-data-lock-point single-subject 80% platelet fall culminating in hospitalisation and corticosteroids (EPAR p92, last paragraph) is assigned here because the source places it in CS3, but it is reported AFTER the CS3 DLP and so is not in any tabulated CS3 denominator. The extension's distinctive finding is that severity is EXPOSURE-DURATION dependent: grade 3/4 events were first detected between week 77 and week 151, i.e. only after CS2 had ended, and thrombocytopenic states lasted longer (41 vs 28 weeks) with longer dose interruptions (8 vs 4.5 weeks), while no event below 25 x10^9/L occurred in either CS3 cohort under weekly monitoring.

studies.study_name: Integrated safety analysis of all inotersen-treated subjects in Studies ISIS 420915-CS2 and ISIS 420915-CS3 ('All Inotersen-Treated (CS2 and CS3) 300 mg', N=161; also reported as the 'Longitudinal Safety Set' and, at an earlier data cut, as 152 subjects)
studies.design: NOT A TRIAL. A sponsor/regulator integrated safety pool combining every subject ever exposed to inotersen across the randomised CS2 trial and its open-label CS3 extension, with subjects followed longitudinally across both protocols on a continuous study-day clock. It has no randomisation, no concurrent control and no protocol of its own; it is an analysis population defined in the Summary of Clinical Safety / Integrated Summary of Safety and reproduced in the FDA Clinical Safety Review and the Tegsedi EPAR.
studies.phase: not applicable (pools a phase 2/3 trial and a phase 3 extension)
studies.indication: hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis with polyneuropathy (hATTR-PN / familial amyloid polyneuropathy)
studies.population: all inotersen-exposed subjects from CS2 and CS3 combined; 161 unique individuals at the 15-Sep-2017 cut
studies.n_enrolled: not applicable - no enrolment of its own. Constituent enrolments: CS2 173 enrolled / 172 dosed, CS3 135 enrolled.
studies.n_analyzed_platelet: 161 at the 15-Sep-2017 Safety Update Report cut (FDA Clinical Safety Review Tables 10, 15 and 24, column 'All Inotersen-Treated (CS2 and CS3) 300 mg (N=161)'), and 152 at an earlier cut (review narrative PDF p155: '23 of 152 (15.1%) inotersen subjects'). CRITICAL NON-ADDITIVITY: 161 = 112 (CS2 inotersen arm) + 49 (CS2 placebo patients first exposed to inotersen in CS3); the 85 CS3 inotersen-inotersen patients are ALREADY inside the 112. 112 + 134 = 246 is therefore wrong by 85 double-counted people. The nested baseline-platelet bands of the longitudinal safety set (N=39 with baseline <200 x10^9/L, N=73 with baseline >=200 x10^9/L, Table 34) sum to 112, i.e. that particular longitudinal analysis follows the CS2 inotersen arm only, not all 161. Do not pool these denominators with each other or with CS2/CS3.
studies.dose_regimen: inotersen 300 mg SC weekly (with the CS2 loading regimen for subjects who started in CS2), plus protocol dose pauses at platelet count <75 x10^9/L and reduced regimens of approximately half dose (150-160 mg weekly or every 2 weeks, and 80 mg weekly or every 2 weeks in one subject) after a pause
studies.duration: cumulative exposure across CS2 and CS3; individual subject trajectories in this pool run to study day 1005 (2 years 9 months) and reduced-dose blocks extend over the last 60 weeks of CS3
studies.platelet_endpoint_basis: "In Studies CS2 and CS3, 23 of 152 (15.1%) inotersen subjects had treatment-emergent moderate to severe thrombocytopenia with a nadir platelet count <75 x10^9/L. (In Study CS2, no placebo-treated subjects had a nadir platelet count <75 x10^9/L.)" [FDA NDA 211172, 211172Orig1s000MedR.pdf, Clinical Safety Review section 8.5.1, narrative preceding Table 32, PDF p155]. The same pool is tabulated across every platelet threshold: "Table 24 ... col 'All Inotersen-Treated (CS2 and CS3) 300 mg (N=161)'" gives <140 x10^9/L 111/161 (68.9%), <100 58/161 (36.0%), <75 31/161 (19.2%), <50 8/161 (5.0%), <25 3/161 (1.9%), >=30% decrease from baseline 134/161 (83.2%) and >=50% decrease 68/161 (42.2%) [FDA review PDF p141]. Scheduled weekly platelet counts under a defined dose-pause rule across both protocols supply the exposure and observation window, so the endpoint was genuinely assessed - but it was assessed inside the two constituent trials, not by this pool.
studies.verification_locus: Constituents are individually identified and independently registry-verified, so rule 3's 'constituents_identifiable = yes' is satisfied without inventing any constituent record: the two constituents are inotersen-CS2-NEURO-TTR (NCT01737398, fetched from https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies/NCT01737398 on 2026-10-01) and inotersen-CS3-OLE (NCT02175004, fetched from https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies/NCT02175004 on 2026-10-01). The pool itself has no registry id and none was invented.
studies.notes: 41 of 198 rows. THIS UNIT IS NOT A TRIAL and must never be counted as one, nor its 161 added to CS2's 112 or CS3's 134. Rows land here when the reported denominator or the stated scope spans both protocols: the seven Table 24 'All Inotersen-Treated (CS2 and CS3) N=161' cells, the Table 34 longitudinal-safety-set baseline-platelet bands, the pooled discontinuation and intracranial-haemorrhage counts from Tables 10 and 15, the 23/152 and 13/23 antibody-association figures, the 27-subject dose-pause tally and the 12-subject reduced-dose tally from Table 35, the 11 subjects with a >=100 to <75 x10^9/L fall within 1-2 weeks, the Table 25 bimodal typology, the TEGSEDI label's 'Study 1 and its extension' 39% figure, and the qualitative CS2+CS3 immune-mechanism statements (anti-platelet IgG present in all grade 3/4 cases, anti-GPIIb/IIIa in 4 of 8, platelet-transfusion refractoriness with corticosteroid response, recurrence in 15 of 16 re-initiated subjects, and failure of dose-frequency reduction in all 4 subjects tried). TWO INDIVIDUAL-SUBJECT TRAJECTORIES are assigned here rather than to CS2 or CS3 because the printed platelet series itself crosses the protocol boundary on a continuous study-day clock and cannot be attributed to one protocol: FDA review Table 29 (61-year-old male, USA, stage 2, nadir 29 x10^9/L on study day 802, with haemoglobin 6.5 g/dL, mental-status change and a possible punctate frontal intraparenchymal haemorrhage, recovering only to 114 x10^9/L) and Table 30 (55-year-old male, USA, stage 1, nadir 43 x10^9/L on study day 1005, with repeated on-drug fall / off-drug rise cycles and persisting thrombocytopenia down to 74 x10^9/L at the halved 160 mg weekly dose). Those two are the cleanest within-subject dechallenge-rechallenge evidence in the whole cluster, and both also show the gradual 'Common' phenotype rather than the fulminant one. The pool's own internal data-cut inconsistency (161 vs 152; 19.2% vs 15.1% for nadir <75 x10^9/L) is preserved as printed.

studies.notes: ONE row (TMSR725) in the whole cluster, and it is the most informative single row for mechanism precisely because it is a negative at short exposure in healthy people: the platelet liability of inotersen is patient- and duration-dependent, not an acute pharmacological effect of the oligonucleotide at the clinical dose. Nothing beyond the quoted sentence and the dose band is asserted here. The lead curator's brief asked for 'any phase 1/2 studies the review describes'; within the four source documents supplied to this cluster, CS1 is the ONLY early-phase study that carries a platelet statement, and no phase 2 study separate from CS2 exists (CS2 is itself registered as phase 2/3). The sponsor's wider programme also includes ISIS 420915-CS4 (EudraCT 2017-005115-13, a NON-INTERVENTIONAL survival-status study in patients who discontinued CS2 or CS3) and ISIS 420915-CS5 (NCT03400098, an ATTR expanded access programme); neither contributes any measurement row to this cluster, so neither was given an evidence unit.

unassignable.why: Not resolvable to any study at any grain, and not an inotersen row at all: oligo_id TOLG060 is DRISAPERSEN. The locus (Tegsedi EPAR p92, AESI 'Thrombocytopenia', opening paragraph) is a SECOND-HAND CITATION of Chi et al. 2017, whose only drisapersen content is the clause 'The latter was also found in clinical studies with other ASOs, e.g. drisapersen.' No study, sponsor code, registry id, phase, population, enrolment, dose, duration, denominator or platelet value is given for drisapersen anywhere at that locus - the row's own notes confirm 'EVERY quantitative field is TBD because this source reports no drisapersen numbers, dose, or study'. Assigning it to any trial would require inventing the trial, and assigning it to a drisapersen evidence unit would create a study record with no verifiable attribute. It is also outside this cluster's compound scope: resolving the drisapersen trials (the GSK/Prosensa DMD programme, e.g. DEMAND III) belongs to a drisapersen cluster working from the primary drisapersen sources, not to a single uninformative cross-reference inside the inotersen EPAR.

notes:
SCOPE AND HEADLINE ANSWER. 198 curated measurement rows in this cluster resolve to just FOUR evidence units, of which only TWO are clinical trials: inotersen-CS2-NEURO-TTR (NCT01737398, verified) and inotersen-CS3-OLE (NCT02175004, verified). The third unit is a regulator/sponsor INTEGRATED SAFETY POOL of those same two trials ('All Inotersen-Treated (CS2 and CS3) 300 mg', N=161) which is NOT a trial, and the fourth is the phase 1 healthy-volunteer study CS1, for which no registry record could be found and whose registry_id is therefore 'TBD'. 197 of 198 rows are assigned; 1 is unassignable. So the trial count for this cluster is 2 registered trials (+1 unregistered-or-unlocated phase 1 healthy-volunteer study, +1 pooled analysis that must not be counted as a trial). 

WHY THE MEASUREMENT-ROW COUNT IS NOT A STUDY COUNT. 126 of the 198 rows (64%) are cells of ONE trial, CS2. They are dose-group, arm, threshold-band, antibody-subgroup, baseline-platelet-band and individual-subject cells of a small number of tables - chiefly FDA Clinical Safety Review Tables 24 (7 cells per cohort column x 4 columns = 28 rows on its own), 31 (6), 33 (15), 34 (4) and 45 (15), plus EPAR section 2.6 and NEJM Table 2. A single table column can generate seven rows. Any analysis that treats rows as independent studies, or as independent observations, will overstate the evidence base by roughly fifty-fold for this compound. 

DEDUPLICATION APPLIED (rule 2). FOUR source documents report the SAME CS2 trial and were collapsed into it: PMID 29972757 (Benson, NEJM 2018), the Tegsedi EPAR EMA/411876/2018 CS2 sections, FDA NDA 211172 211172Orig1s000MedR.pdf CS2 columns, and the TEGSEDI US label. NO label_summary evidence unit was created, because the label's section 5.1 platelet figures are not an independent evidence unit: 25% below 100 x10^9/L, 14% below 75 x10^9/L, 3% below 25 x10^9/L and 3 antibody-positive severe cases reproduce FDA review Table 24 and narrative p142 for the same 112 CS2 patients, and the label's 39% figure for nadir <75 x10^9/L in patients with baseline platelets <200 x10^9/L is the CS2+CS3 longitudinal pool (38.5%, Table 34), so it was assigned to the pooled unit. The boxed-warning death is the same Argentinian CS2 subject as NEJM's fatal intracranial haemorrhage, FDA review Figure 2 / Table 26, and EPAR p93. QUANTIFIED: NINE separate measurement rows in this cluster describe that ONE patient - TMSR717 (EPAR p102, fatal ICH attributable to thrombocytopenia), TMSR777 (EPAR p93, nadir <10 x10^9/L), TMSR791 (FDA Figure 2, treatment-emergent IgG on day 87), TMSR813 (FDA Table 10, CS2 intracranial haemorrhage 1/112), TMSR848 (FDA Table 26, platelets <10 x10^9/L on study day 121), TMSR900 (FDA Table 8, death 0.9%), TMSR906 (label boxed warning), TMSR914 (NEJM Results, platelet count <10,000/mm3) and TMSR927 (NEJM Table 2, intracranial haemorrhage). A tenth row, TMSR812 (FDA Table 10, 2/161 pooled), contains him plus one unrelated anticoagulant-associated subarachnoid haemorrhage, and TMSR920 (NEJM, '2 of these 3 patients' recovered) is defined by his non-recovery. The three patients who fell below 25 x10^9/L are likewise reported four times over (EPAR 2.7%, FDA Table 24 2.7%, NEJM 3%, label 3% - all 3/112), and the CS2 <100 and <75 x10^9/L rates appear twice each (FDA Table 24 25.0% / 14.3%; label 25% / 14%). One genuine near-miss worth keeping distinct rather than merging: NEJM's 54% below 140 x10^9/L is 60/112 CONFIRMED decreases, while FDA Table 24's 55.4% is 62/112 ANY post-baseline value, so those two are different endpoint definitions, not a transcription discrepancy. 

THE DENOMINATOR TRAP, STATED EXPLICITLY (rule 7). The three headline denominators OVERLAP and must never be summed: CS2 = 112 inotersen (+60 placebo); CS3 = 134 analysed (85 inotersen-inotersen + 49 placebo-inotersen); pooled = 161. The arithmetic proves the overlap: 161 = 112 + 49, i.e. the pooled 'all inotersen-treated' population is the CS2 inotersen arm plus the CS2 placebo patients who crossed over in CS3, and the 85 CS3 inotersen-inotersen patients are already inside the 112. Summing 112 + 134 = 246 double-counts 85 real people. A further trap: the Table 34 longitudinal-safety-set baseline bands (N=39 and N=73) sum to 112, not 161, so that particular 'CS2 and CS3' analysis follows only the CS2 inotersen arm across both protocols.

CS1 AND WHY IT IS 'TBD' NOT 'NOT_REGISTERED'. ClinicalTrials.gov searches on 'ISIS 420915', '420915', 'ISIS-TTRRx', 'IONIS-TTR' and intervention 'inotersen' returned only CS2, CS3 and CS5 (NCT03400098, expanded access) for this sponsor code; the EU CTR returned CS2, CS3 and CS4 (2017-005115-13, non-interventional) and no CS1. Europe PMC identifies the publication of the phase 1 healthy-volunteer study (Ackermann et al., Amyloid 2016;23:148-157, PMID 27355239), which cites no registry number. Phase 1 healthy-volunteer studies fall outside mandatory FDAAA 801 registration, so non-registration is plausible - but that is not the positive establishment rule 1 requires, so 'TBD' is used and the searches are recorded in the unit's verification_locus. 

PLATELET-ENDPOINT EVALUABILITY (rule 5). CS2, CS3 and the pool are rated 'yes': all three carry scheduled, protocol-defined platelet counts (amended to WEEKLY in CS2 after the fatal event, weekly throughout CS3) with a defined dose-pause rule at <75 x10^9/L, and verbatim tabulated threshold distributions are quoted in each unit's platelet_endpoint_basis. CS1 is rated 'partial': the EPAR affirms that platelets were examined ('No consistent effect on platelets was seen in the Phase 1 study with multiple dosing') but gives no denominator, value, schedule or protocol endpoint. NO NEGATIVE WAS FABRICATED anywhere: the explicit zeros in the input (0% placebo dose holds, 0% placebo 'platelet count decreased', 0/85 and 0/49 below 25 x10^9/L in the CS3 cohorts, 0 placebo intracranial haemorrhages, 0 placebo serious thrombocytopenia, 0 prothrombin-time prolongation, 'No cases of thrombocytopenia with platelet counts of less than 50,000 per cubic millimeter occurred after the institution of weekly platelet monitoring') are all tabulated or explicitly stated measured values at a named locus, not inferences from silence. 

INDIVIDUAL-SUBJECT ROWS ARE NOT CASE REPORTS. Six subject-level trajectories appear in the input (FDA review Figure 2 and Tables 26-30). None was typed 'case_report': every one is a randomised trial subject whose data are reported inside the CS2/CS3 safety review. Four sit wholly within CS2 (the fatal Argentinian case, the Italian nadir-9 case, the Brazilian nadir-5 case, and the CS2 subject who fell from 100 to 40 x10^9/L in one week) and are assigned to CS2; two have platelet series that cross the CS2/CS3 boundary on a continuous study-day clock (nadir 29 on day 802, nadir 43 on day 1005 with on/off rechallenge cycles and persistent thrombocytopenia at the halved 160 mg dose) and are assigned to the integrated pool, because attributing them to a single protocol would be a guess. 

DISCREPANCIES PRESERVED. Source-internal inconsistencies were recorded, not reconciled: >=30% decrease from baseline in CS2 is 75.0% (Table 24) vs 71% (reviewer comment after Table 34); nadir <75 x10^9/L in CS2 is 14.3% (16/112, 15-Sep-2017 cut) vs 11.6% (13/112, 28-Mar-2017 cut); the pooled nadir <75 figure is 19.2% (31/161) vs 15.1% (23/152); the CS2 dose-hold rate is 11% (EPAR p88) vs 'approximately 10%' (EPAR p93/p113/p128); the AE incidence is 13% for PT 'Thrombocytopenia' alone vs 24% for that PT combined with 'Platelet count decreased'; discontinuation for thrombocytopenia is 5.4% (EPAR p92) vs 4.5% (EPAR p110); NEJM Table 2 lists 2 serious thrombocytopenia events while its abstract says 3; and the EPAR itself disagrees with itself on whether CS3 showed a further mean platelet decline (p93 'no further significant mean reductions' vs p112 'CS3 Week 39: mean platelet counts reduced by 28.5% from CS2 baseline'). 

ONE UNASSIGNABLE ROW. TMSR526 is a drisapersen row (oligo_id TOLG060), not an inotersen row, and is a second-hand citation inside the Tegsedi EPAR with every quantitative field TBD and no study named. It cannot be resolved to a study without inventing one.
